opus.title: split `mode: wipe` fails the --layers stack check unless the shot happens to have a caption; the divider wrapper fades and moves by transform
opus.root_cause: split.js:95 creates the divider wrapper with opacity:0, and :143-144 fade it while moving it with translateX. Its children's box-shadows hang outside it. That is the GUIDE's own 'moves by transform and fades' trap, so Chrome composites the divider in f0–f5, and the other layers then rasterise differently from the flattened clip.
opus.evidence: I re-ran it on a copy of Sonnet's p8 (snapshot copy): `lv.mjs --job p8 --layers wa --aspect 9x16` gives FAIL stack 8/71 (f0 2969 px, f2 8470, f4 8692; composited in ref-alpha, ref-opaque and divider), rc=1. The numbers are identical to Sonnet's run, so this is deterministic. With the patched split.js (wrapper unfaded, both children faded, positioned by `left`), the same command gives PASS stack and stack+bg, worst f52 0 px > 16, max diff 4, rc=0. GUIDE.md:537-538 claims every built-in block avoids these triggers except panel glass.
opus.fix: split.js: create the divider without opacity, set opacity on its two child divs in render, and position it with `divider.style.left = divider._.x0 + px` instead of a transform. Correct GUIDE.md:537 and add a bare wipe and a text+wipe to the layers regression set. Re-verify 16:9 and 1:1, and the reel-sample s6 layers. Film pixels around the divider change only at antialiasing level (a new block, so no old jobs).

sonnet.title: split mode: wipe fails the --layers stack check in almost every configuration; only the shipped sample's exact config passes, with a thin margin
sonnet.failure_scenario: `--layers` on a wipe shot gives `FAIL stack` ("Chrome composited part of the frame on its own") unless the shot has a caption and nothing else (the reel-sample s6 shape). Bare wipe, wipe + `text` headline, wipe + `bg`, wipe with footage fields, and the full-featured wipe all FAIL, in early frames f0–f6 with up to 26k px off (max diff 131). GUIDE.md:537-538 claims the built-in blocks avoid every listed compositing trigger except panel glass; REPORTS.md says the sample's layers pass (margin 36/64).
sonnet.evidence: 9:16, `node work/REEL/s/video/lv.mjs --job work/REEL/p8 --layers <id>`: wa (bare wipe) FAIL 8/71 frames (f0 2969 px, f2 8470 px); wb (+text) FAIL 17/70; wc (+bg) FAIL 8/71; wd (caption only) PASS worst f17 36 px (max diff 83); stress job t4 (text+caption+bg+labels) FAIL 21/85; p6 v4 (video before/after) FAIL 8/85; reel-sample s6 copy (work/REEL/rs) PASS at 36 px. Logs: work/REEL/p8/layers_w{a,b,c,d}.log, rs/layers_s6.log, p6/layers916.log. Root cause found with a CDP LayerTree probe (work/REEL/lt3.mjs): the `divider` wrapper (92x1061) and its handle (165x165) are composited by Chrome in f0–f4.5 (opacity 0) and again from f8.5 on, also in the sample. split.js:95 creates the wrapper with `opacity:0` and 143-144 fades the wrapper while moving it with `transform: translateX` — exactly the GUIDE trap "moves by transform and fades" plus box-shadow children hanging outside a fading box. Probe: moving by `left` alone still composites while opacity<1; `left` + fading the two children (wrapper stays opacity 1) leaves zero composited layers in 9:16, 16:9 and 1:1. Same side mode (kit s3 1x1, p6 v2), float, sticker, cta, media layers all PASS, so this is specific to the wipe divider.
sonnet.suggested_fix: In split.js: create the divider wrapper without opacity, set `opacity` on its two child divs in render, and position it with `style.left = divider._.x0 + px` instead of transform. Verified in a patched copy (work/REEL/s2): `--layers wa,wb` PASS worst 0 px > 16 (was FAIL), and the reel-sample wipe improves from 36 px to 0 px. Cost: film pixels around the divider change at antialiasing level (it stops being a separately rasterised layer; max diff 138 on its thin edges, ~66 over the frame at f4), so this is a visual-noise change, not a look change. Also correct GUIDE.md:537 and add a wipe-without-caption case to the layers regression set.

opus.title: `captionAt` is unvalidated: "1.5s"/"abc" → NaN hero frame and a raw TypeError after --grid passed; a value past the shot silently drops the caption
opus.root_cause: reelCapPlan (_reel.js:194) uses Number(s.captionAt ?? 4), so seconds strings become NaN. NaN flows to hero() (Math.max(30, NaN) = NaN), then to timeline heroF (timeline.mjs:89), then to render(NaN), where reelShaker reads J[NaN][0]. spec.mjs never checks captionAt, while every other time field accepts '1.5s' through K.frameAt.
opus.evidence: work/opus-enginereel/cap1 (sticker, `caption: Pick a style now, captionAt: 1.5s`). --grid prints a normal table with no warning. compile() gives `heroF NaN`. `--storyboard --aspect 9x16` gives `✗ page.evaluate: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '0')`, which names neither the shot nor the field.
opus.fix: _reel.js: import frameAt from ../kit.js (it is isomorphic) and use `start = frameAt(s.captionAt) ?? 4`. spec.mjs: for any shot with `caption`, validate captionAt with isAt and warn when it is ≥ Db. timeline.mjs:89: if hero() is not finite, throw a UserError naming the block and shot. Numeric captionAt renders exactly as now.

sonnet.title: `captionAt` is never validated: "1.5s"/"abc" give a NaN hero frame and a raw stack-trace crash after --grid passed; a value past the shot end silently drops the caption
sonnet.failure_scenario: Every other time-like field (pan.at, overlays at/until, roster first, sidebar at) accepts a frame number or "1.5s" and is checked at --grid, but `captionAt: 1.5s` or `captionAt: abc` is read as Number(...) = NaN (_reel.js:194). --grid prints a normal table, then --storyboard/--film die with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '0')` at _reel.js:167 (sticker/cta, via the NaN-keyed shaker) or `page errors while loading the stage: <feGaussianBlur> attribute stdDeviation: Expected number, "NaN NaN"` (float/split/media) — neither names the shot or the field. `captionAt: 400` on a 2.8 s shot passes silently: words never pop, the only warning is a nonsense "pops 12.0 words/s".
sonnet.evidence: work/REEL/p3, p2: sticker `caption: Hello world today`, `captionAt: 1.5s` and `abc` -> `lv.mjs --grid` rc=0 no warnings; `--storyboard --aspect 9x16` -> "✗ page.evaluate: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '0') at _reel.js:168:19". Same value on float/split/media -> the feGaussianBlur NaN page error. `captionAt: 400` -> storyboard renders with no caption and only "pops 12.0 words/s". Contrast: `cardFrom: abc` IS rejected at --grid ("cardFrom must be seconds ≥ 0"). spec.mjs has no captionAt check (grep). Cause chain: NaN start -> reelCapPlan.end NaN -> hero() NaN -> sh.heroF NaN (timeline.mjs:89) -> render(NaN).
sonnet.suggested_fix: In spec.mjs, for any shot with `caption`, validate `captionAt` with the same isAt/K.frameAt path as pan.at (frames or "1.5s", finite, ≥ 0) and warn/error when it is ≥ the shot length; have reelCapPlan use K.frameAt. Also guard reelShaker (k NaN) and timeline heroF with Number.isFinite so a bad value can never become a stack trace.

opus.title: sticker `tilt` is unvalidated: `tilt: -5deg` silently renders a ~56 % size, untilted sticker
opus.root_cause: Number('-5deg') is NaN. reelEnvelope(…, NaN) gives NaN bounds, so `env.w <= A.w` is never true and the fit loop runs to it=7 (k = .92^7 ≈ .56). The nudge `nx || ny` is NaN and falsy, so nothing moves, and reelXf's `g.rot || 0` turns the rotation into 0.
opus.evidence: Code path read end to end: sticker.js:44, :69-79, :81-82; _reel.js:157. Sonnet's DOM measure (p20): one line at ≈103 px font with 0° rotation, against two lines at ≈184 px and −4.5°. No warning at --grid.
opus.fix: spec.mjs: `tilt` must be a finite number in −45…45 (built-in sticker), error otherwise. sticker.js: Number.isFinite guard falling back to −5. Numeric tilts render unchanged.

sonnet.title: sticker `tilt` is unvalidated: `tilt: -5deg` silently renders a ~56 % size, untilted sticker
sonnet.failure_scenario: `tilt` is documented as "degrees (default −5)". A user who writes `tilt: -5deg` (or any non-number) gets Number(...) = NaN: the fit loop's envelope test is NaN so it never passes and shrinks the lockup 8 times (×0.92 each), and reelXf's `g.rot || 0` turns the NaN rotation into 0. Output: a flat sticker at about half size, no warning at --grid, no error at render.
sonnet.evidence: work/REEL/p20 (same text, tilt -5deg vs -5), DOM at f30: title line height 110 px, one line (font ≈103 px) for `-5deg` vs two 197 px lines (font ≈184 px) for `-5`; computed rotation 0deg vs -4.5deg. `--grid` on p5 prints no warning for tilt -5deg; storyboard (work/REEL/p5/reel-storyboard-9x16.png) shows k1 visibly smaller and flat next to k2/k3. Code: sticker.js:44 Number(s.tilt ?? -5), :76-77 envelope loop, _reel.js:157 (g.rot || 0).
sonnet.suggested_fix: Validate `tilt` in spec.mjs (finite number, e.g. −45…45; optionally strip a trailing `deg`) and add a Number.isFinite guard in sticker.js so a bad value falls back to the default with a --grid error instead of a silent shrink.

opus.title: A caption with a standalone `*` passes --grid and aborts the render ('report this caption')
opus.root_cause: reelWords replaces every * and | with a space before counting. ctx.text tokenises through K.parseCopy, which keeps an unpaired `*` (or `**`) as a word span, so the timing count and the on-screen count disagree.
opus.evidence: work/opus-enginereel/cap2: `caption: "Terms * apply now"`. --grid is clean; `--storyboard --aspect 9x16` gives `✗ stage failed to build: … sticker a1: caption has 4 words on screen but 3 in its timing — report this caption`.
opus.fix: Make reelWords use the same tokenizer as ctx.text: `parseCopy(c).flatMap(p => p.br ? [] : p.text.split(/\s+/)).filter(Boolean)`. Counts are unchanged for every caption without a lone or double star, so there is no pixel change.

sonnet.title: A caption containing a standalone `*` passes --grid and then aborts the render with "report this caption"
sonnet.failure_scenario: reelWords() (line 8) turns every `*` into a space, but ctx.text renders a lone `*` token as a word. For `caption: Terms * apply now` the timing counts 3 words and the page has 4, so build throws "sticker a1: caption has 4 words on screen but 3 in its timing — report this caption" at --storyboard/--film. --grid is clean. Same for any reel block and media with a caption.
sonnet.evidence: work/REEL/p1 (sticker a1). `lv.mjs --grid` rc=0; `--storyboard --aspect 9x16` -> "✗ stage failed to build: page.evaluate: Error: sticker a1: caption has 4 words on screen but 3 in its timing — report this caption". Footnote-style `Free*` (star attached to a word) is fine; only a space-separated `*` token mismatches.
sonnet.suggested_fix: Make reelWords count exactly what ctx.text renders: tokenise with K.parseCopy(...) and split on whitespace (one shared tokenizer for Node and browser), instead of regex-replacing `*|`.

opus.title: Docs: 'leave bg off → transparent overlays' gives a fully opaque cta clip (its glow backdrop is block content); QA correctly passes it
opus.root_cause: cta.js:37-44 draws a dark glow backdrop as content when the shot has no bg. GUIDE.md:320 and reel.yaml:5 tell the user to keep shots bg-less for overlays, without the cta exception (`bg: none`).
opus.evidence: cta.js:37 checks `!ctx.hasBg && String(s.bg ?? '') !== 'none'`. qa.mjs:239-241 deliberately accepts fully opaque alpha clips (full-bleed media are saved as RGB), so QA is not wrong. The only defect is the guidance. Sonnet: kit s7 clip is 100 % opaque, while with `bg: none` it is 4.1 % opaque.
opus.fix: GUIDE.md:320 and reel.yaml:5: add '(cta: `bg: none`)'. Optionally have qaClip print INFO when an --alpha clip is opaque in every frame. No render change.

sonnet.category: docs vs behaviour / QA blind spot
sonnet.title: A bg-less cta exports as a fully opaque clip under `--clips --alpha`; QA passes it and GUIDE.md:320 / the reel starter header say to leave bg off for overlays
sonnet.failure_scenario: GUIDE.md:320 ("leave bg off … export the graphics as transparent overlays") and templates/reel.yaml:5 ("keep the shots bg-less and export them as overlays") lead a user to `--clips all --alpha`; the starter's s7 cta has no bg, so its clip is a solid dark frame with drifting glows (the glow backdrop is block content, cta.js:37-44). Only the cta table row, the block doc and an s7 comment say `bg: none` is the overlay form. qaClip's alpha check (qa.mjs:241) only requires some alpha ≥ 40, so an all-opaque 'transparent' clip is PASS.
sonnet.evidence: work/REEL/kit: `lv.mjs --job kit --clips s7 --alpha --aspect 9x16` -> PASS clip/content/freeze; alpha plane at frame 40 is 100 % opaque (PIL: opaque share 1.0). Control, stress job: cta with `bg: none` -> 4.1 % opaque (transparent as documented); sticker over `bg:` footage -> 1.9 % opaque (footage left out). Layers for the no-bg cta (backdrop layer) PASS in 9:16 and 16:9.
sonnet.suggested_fix: Say "(cta: bg: none)" in GUIDE.md:320 and the reel.yaml header, and have qaClip print an INFO/WARN when an --alpha clip has no transparent pixel in any frame (with a cta hint).

opus.title: Reel boolean fields accept anything: `sparks: no`, `gloss: off`, `shake: "false"` leave the effect on; typos are silently ignored
opus.root_cause: sticker.js:44/46/103, cta logo, split arrow and float streak test only `=== false`. The yaml 1.2 parser reads no/off as strings. spec.mjs type-checks agent's `dolly` (:220) but none of the reel booleans. Unknown-key warnings are a gap for every block, including PRE, so that part is not a regression.
opus.evidence: Code read: sticker.js:44 `shake = s.shake !== false`, :46 `s.sparks === false`, :103 `s.gloss === false`; spec.mjs ENUMS (:33-40) has no boolean entries; spec.mjs:220 has the dolly check for comparison. Sonnet's p5/p19 storyboards show the effects still on.
opus.fix: spec.mjs: for built-in sticker/cta/split/float, `shake/sparks/gloss/logo/arrow/streak` must be true or false, with an error like `(got "no")`. An unknown-key warning with did-you-mean is optional.

sonnet.title: Reel boolean fields and misspelled fields are silently ignored
sonnet.failure_scenario: Only a literal YAML `false` switches shake/sparks/gloss/arrow/streak/logo off (sticker.js:44/46/103, split arrow, float streak, cta logo): with the yaml 1.2 parser `sparks: no`, `gloss: off`, `shake: "false"` are strings, so the effect stays ON. Typos such as `ribon:`, `capton:`, `captionat:` are also accepted with no warning, so the element just never appears. ENUMS (spec.mjs:33: style/pos/mode/device/from) are the only checked reel params.
sonnet.evidence: work/REEL/p5 shot k3 (`shake: "false"`, `sparks: "no"`, `gloss: off`) -> storyboard still shows the sparkles; work/REEL/p19 (`ribon`, `captionat`, `capton`, `titl` next to valid `caption`/`kicker`) -> `--grid` rc=0, no warning, the ribbon and the second caption are simply absent from the "on screen" column.
sonnet.suggested_fix: Type-check booleans for the reel blocks (error "must be true or false (got \"no\")"), and warn on unknown shot keys using block.params plus the common-field list from --blocks, with a did-you-mean.

opus.title: Word-pop captions split only on spaces: a CJK caption is one 'word' (appears at once, plate over the whole line), and nothing warns
opus.root_cause: reelWords and ctx.text both split on \s, so a CJK sentence is a single inline-block .lv-w span. The reading-time check also counts it as one word.
opus.evidence: Code: _reel.js:8 and runtime.js:246 both split on whitespace. Sonnet's p11 storyboard shows a 31-character caption at once with the plate behind the whole first line.
opus.fix: Document the limit and warn at --grid when a caption has more than ~12 characters with no spaces. An Intl.Segmenter tokenizer in both places is a feature, and would change only CJK captions.

sonnet.title: Word-pop captions only split on spaces, so CJK captions do not pop word by word and the accent plate spans a whole line
sonnet.failure_scenario: A Chinese caption has no spaces, so reelWords() counts 1 word: the whole sentence appears at once and the highlight plate covers the first full line. Nothing in GUIDE says captions need space-separated text, and the reading-time check also counts it as 1 word.
sonnet.evidence: work/REEL/p11 (a 31-character Chinese `caption:`): the storyboard shows both lines at once with the purple plate behind the whole first line; --grid raises no warning. Space-separated CJK sticker text and cta words render fine.
sonnet.suggested_fix: Tokenise with Intl.Segmenter (word granularity) in the shared tokenizer, or document the limit and warn at --grid when a caption is longer than ~12 characters with no spaces.

opus.title: cta emits the pre/post pop SFX even when `pre`/`post` are empty
opus.root_cause: cues() always pushes pops at CT.pre+1 and CT.post+1, but build skips empty lines (mkLine returns null for '').
opus.evidence: cta.js:31 is unconditional; cta.js:46 and :52 skip empty copy; the logo pop is conditional on `logo !== false` but pre/post are not. Sonnet's p17 compile shows the pops at 0.23 s and 0.33 s with nothing on screen.
opus.fix: Build the cue list from `pre = s.pre ?? 'Comment'` and `post = s.post ?? 'to get the link'` and skip a pop whose text is empty. Same in sheet.mjs:89.

sonnet.title: cta still emits the pre/post pop SFX when `pre`/`post` are empty
sonnet.failure_scenario: `pre: ""` / `post: ""` correctly draw no line (build and copy() both skip them), but cues() always emits pops at frames 7 and 10, so two clicks play with nothing appearing; the review sheet line (lib/sheet.mjs:89) prints `"" / "" slide in`. The logo pop is conditioned on `logo !== false`; pre/post are not.
sonnet.evidence: work/REEL/p17: shot with `pre: ""`, `post: ""`, `logo: false` -> compile() copy ["GO"], cues hit@0.03s pop@0.23s pop@0.33s pop@0.60s; default cta -> hit + 4 pops.
sonnet.suggested_fix: Build the cue list from the same `pre ?? 'Comment'` / `post ?? 'to get the link'` values and skip the pop when the text is empty; same in sheet.mjs.

opus.title: float `text` param doc says 'beside the card on landscape'; the code puts it beside only for a tall card (ar < 1.6) or a phone
opus.root_cause: Doc string out of step with float.js:54 `side = text && !portrait && (phone || (!square && ar < 1.6))`.
opus.evidence: float.js:26 against float.js:49-54. The code comment at :49 states the real rule.
opus.fix: Reword the param: 'beside a tall card or a phone on landscape (a phone on square); above a wide card and on portrait'.

sonnet.title: float `text` param doc says the headline sits beside the card on landscape; code only does that for a tall card or a phone
sonnet.failure_scenario: `text: optional sticker headline (beside the card on landscape, above it otherwise)` shows in `--blocks`; float.js:54 puts it beside only when `!portrait && (phone || (!square && ar < 1.6))`, so a normal wide screenshot on 16:9 stacks the headline above the card (the code comment at line 49 and the reel-sample note say so). A user composing for 16:9 from the param text expects a side-by-side layout.
sonnet.evidence: work/REEL/s1 t3 (phone, beside) vs work/REEL/p4 f1 / p10 l3 (wide card in 16:9 -> headline above), storyboards in those folders.
sonnet.suggested_fix: Reword to "beside the card for a tall card or a phone on landscape (a phone on square); above it for a wide card and on portrait".

opus.title: New params aren't validated. `captionAt: 0.5s` crashes the stage; boolean options set to no/off/0 silently stay on; `through: yes` silently does nothing; `push` is unbounded; a list in a single-path footage field fails only at stage build
opus.root_cause: spec.mjs has no captionAt check. _reel.js:194 does Number(s.captionAt ?? 4), so 0.5s becomes NaN. Blocks test `=== false`, and YAML 1.2 parses no/off as strings and 0 as a number. type.js:9 `thr` maps any non-true value through Number(), so 'yes' becomes 0. push only gets num(). mediaFields() can't tell list fields from single-path fields.
opus.evidence: work/opus-libtoolsdocs/cap (sticker caption, `captionAt: 0.5s`): grid rc 0, then storyboard fails with 'page errors … <feGaussianBlur> attribute stdDeviation: Expected number, "NaN NaN"'. Every other timing field in the skill accepts seconds. work/opus-libtoolsdocs/bool (`shake: no, sparks: off, gloss: 0`, `through: yes`, `push: 99`): grid rc 0, and loadSpec keeps ['no','off',0], 'yes' and 99. The code tests are sticker.js:21/44/46/103/114, float.js:44, split.js:38/74, cta.js:32/62, lockup.js:25, type.js:9/52. Only agent.dolly is type-checked (spec.mjs:220).
opus.fix: In spec.mjs, for built-in blocks: (a) check captionAt with isAt and convert seconds via K.frameAt in _reel.reelCapPlan; (b) accept only true/false for the documented on/off options (shake, sparks, gloss, streak, arrow, logo, overLogo, backdrop) and for `through` (true/false or a frame count > 0 and < D), naming the field; (c) bound push, e.g. −0.5…0.5; (d) give mediaFields a `list` flag so a list in card/before/after, or a non-string list item, is a --grid error. No pixel change for valid jobs.

sonnet.title: Several new params are not validated: `captionAt` (crashes the page), boolean options that silently stay ON for no/off/0, unbounded `push`, a list in a single-path footage field
sonnet.failure_scenario: `captionAt: 0.5s` (every other timing field in the skill accepts seconds) passes --grid and then crashes the stage with a TypeError; `captionAt: soon` gives NaN SVG errors. `shake: no`, `sparks: off`, `gloss: 0` parse as the strings 'no'/'off' or 0 (YAML 1.2), are not `=== false`, and the effect silently stays on. `push: 99` is accepted (100x zoom). `float card: [a.png, b.png]` or a dangling `- ` in `stack cards` passes --grid and fails only when the stage builds.
sonnet.evidence: work/LIB/fz/capAt_secs (sticker caption + `captionAt: 0.5s`): `--grid` rc 0; `--storyboard` rc 1 `page.evaluate: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '0') at _reel.js:168:19`. work/LIB/fz/sticker_caption_at (`captionAt: soon`): `Error: <feGaussianBlur> attribute stdDeviation: Expected number, "NaN NaN"`. _reel.js:194 `Number(s.captionAt ?? 4)`; no captionAt check anywhere in spec.mjs although media, sticker, split, float and cta all take it. Booleans: `yaml.parse('shake: no\nsparks: off\ngloss: 0')` -> {shake:'no', sparks:'off', gloss:0}; grid accepts (fz/bool_off rc 0); code tests `=== false`: sticker.js:21,44,46,103,114; float.js:44; split.js:38,74; cta.js:32,62; lockup.js:25; type.js:52. Only agent.dolly got a boolean check (spec.mjs:220). `push` check is `num()` only (spec.mjs:184; fz/push_99 rc 0). Lists: fz/float_card_list -> `stage failed to build: shot a: assets/a.png,assets/b.png could not be decoded as an image` + HTTP 404; fz/split_before_null_in_list -> `shot a: null could not be decoded as an image`; mediaFields() (spec.mjs:19) cannot tell list fields from single-path fields so spec.mjs:283-288 accepts both shapes for any field.
sonnet.suggested_fix: Validate captionAt with the same isAt()/frameAt rule (and convert seconds) for blocks that list a caption param; reject non-boolean values for the known on/off options (allow true/false only, name the field); bound push (e.g. -0.5..0.5); let mediaFields() carry `list: true|false` so a list in a scalar field (or a non-string item) is a clear --grid error.
